open_points.subject: Owner / staff
open_points.text: “Owner / staff” and “They authenticate with a staff credential”
open_points.question: Are the owner and staff distinct actors, who may become staff, and does possession of the shared staff credential alone make a caller staff?
options: The owner plus explicitly authorised human staff
Any human or tool holding the staff credential acts as staff
open_points.default_guess: Treat the owner and explicitly authorised people or tools holding the shared credential as staff.

open_points.subject: Personal-data trust boundary
open_points.text: “Personal data — the customer's contact data (R0-06); readable by staff only (R0-09)” contradicts “every contact field it records or reads passes to the provider of the model the owner runs it on”
open_points.question: Does “readable by staff only” describe only Registry API authorization, allowing an external model provider to receive the data, or is disclosure to any non-staff party prohibited?
options: Staff-only applies only at the Registry API boundary; the selected model provider is an accepted recipient
Model providers must be treated as staff actors
Contact data must not be sent to a model provider
open_points.default_guess: Interpret staff-only as an API authorization rule and treat the owner's selected model provider as an accepted external data recipient.

open_points.subject: Browser and staff credential
open_points.text: “The Registry frontend calls the API from the browser” and “How the frontend obtains the staff credential belongs to the frontend”, while R0-23 names “the operator, a frontend server” as tools holding the credential
open_points.question: For the direct same-host browser flow, is the browser itself allowed to receive and hold the staff credential, or must staff actions always pass through a credential-holding server?
options: The browser may hold and present the credential
All staff writes pass through a frontend server
The direct browser frontend is read-only
open_points.default_guess: Allow the same-host browser to hold the credential transiently and present it directly.

open_points.subject: Operator host access and service-token boundary
open_points.text: “it holds no service token” conflicts with “An agent works with the owner's own access to Registry's host” and configuration being “readable only by the owner and the Registry process”
open_points.question: Does the operator's use of the owner's host access permit it to read Registry configuration and thereby obtain service tokens, or is its filesystem access technically restricted away from secrets?
options: The operator has full owner-level access and is inside the trust boundary for all configured secrets
The operator is technically prevented from reading Registry configuration
The operator can read configuration but is only procedurally forbidden to use service tokens
open_points.default_guess: Treat the operator as having owner-level technical access to configured secrets, while using only its provisioned staff credential for API calls.
